info.title: meshy/rigging
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "meshy/rigging", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description: Request body for Meshy's rigging operation (docs.meshy.ai/en/api/rigging): fit a skeleton to an existing humanoid mesh. Supply exactly one of input_task_id or model_url; Meshy requires no single field, so the only structural narrowing is that an empty body is refused.

height_meters.description: The approximate height of the character model in meters. Must be a positive number.

input_task_id.description: The input task that needs to be rigged. Required if model_url is not provided.

model_url.description: A publicly accessible URL or Data URI to a textured humanoid GLB file. Required if input_task_id is not provided.

texture_image_url.description: The model's UV-unwrapped base color texture image. Publicly accessible URL or Data URI. Supports .png format.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for Meshy's rigging operation: the terminal `GET /proxy/meshy/openapi/v1/rigging/{task_id}` task document, forwarded unchanged. The operation is SUBMIT-AND-POLL — `POST /proxy/meshy/openapi/v1/rigging` answers a `MeshyRiggingCreateResponse` handle whose `result` is the task id and which carries no asset, and Router polls on the caller's behalf — so the body a caller receives is the finished task document rather than that handle.
`meshy/rigging` names an OPERATION rather than a model version: it adds a skeleton to a mesh the caller already has (a preceding task's id or a model URL), so it consumes a 3D asset and produces one. It is not one of the text-to-3D generations.
The output is under `result`, and this operation shares NO output key with the other Meshy operations. `result.rigged_character_glb_url` and `result.rigged_character_fbx_url` are the rigged character itself. `result.basic_animations` carries six further URLs — a walking and a running clip, each as a skinned GLB, a skinned FBX and an armature GLB. Which of the eight are populated depends on the request, so read the one that is present. Comfy Router draws that line: a `SUCCEEDED` task carrying none of those eight URLs is answered as a Comfy Router error rather than with this document. Note that `result.basic_animations` being present is NOT itself evidence of output — an empty object is representable and carries nothing loadable.
`status` is the shared Meshy UPPERCASE vocabulary — `PENDING`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELED` — forwarded unchanged. `SUCCEEDED` is the one terminal success; `FAILED` and `CANCELED` reach a Router caller as a Comfy Router error with Meshy's own reason in `task_error.message`. `progress` runs 0..100. `expires_at` is when Meshy stops serving the result URLs, so fetch them rather than storing the document.

running_armature_glb_url.description: Downloadable URL for running animation armature in GLB format.

running_fbx_url.description: Downloadable URL for running animation in FBX format (with skin).

running_glb_url.description: Downloadable URL for running animation in GLB format (with skin).

walking_armature_glb_url.description: Downloadable URL for walking animation armature in GLB format.

walking_fbx_url.description: Downloadable URL for walking animation in FBX format (with skin).

walking_glb_url.description: Downloadable URL for walking animation in GLB format (with skin).

MeshyRiggingResult.description: Contains the output asset URLs if the task SUCCEEDED.

rigged_character_fbx_url.description: Downloadable URL for the rigged character in FBX format.

rigged_character_glb_url.description: Downloadable URL for the rigged character in GLB format.

created_at.description: Timestamp of when the task was created, in milliseconds.

expires_at.description: Timestamp of when the task result expires, in milliseconds.

finished_at.description: Timestamp of when the task was finished, in milliseconds. 0 if not finished.

preceding_tasks.description: The count of preceding tasks. Only meaningful when status is PENDING.

progress.description: Progress of the task (0-100). 0 if not started, 100 if succeeded.

started_at.description: Timestamp of when the task was started, in milliseconds. 0 if not started.

MeshyTaskError.description: Error object that contains the error message if the task failed.
